{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOU4GkE88AAAABi5a9Zw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlaE0zhMPuy8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlaE0", "number": 62, "title": "Experiment with a task-fine-tuned lightweight local LLM for AI Livestream comments", "body": "## Background

The browser-local AI Livestream demo (`projects/ai-livestream/`) still has disappointing short-chat quality even on a capable Mac. On a Pixel 7a the current model also places an impractical load on the device. The user wants to test **a smaller, task-specific, genuinely fine-tuned generative language model** as the **first isolated experiment**, rather than starting with video, ASR, or UI optimizations.

Current baseline: Whisper Base q8 / WASM for speech recognition, and `mlc-ai/Qwen3-1.7B-q4f16_1-MLC` via WebLLM / WebGPU for comment generation (approximately 1.1 GB total initial assets). Previous evaluations are in `projects/ai-livestream/MODEL-EVALUATION.md` and existing synthetic fixtures/tests. The app is a **simulated private livestream**, with no remote speech or text inference.

## Goal

**Actually train or adapt a smaller LLM specifically to produce natural, short, topic-relevant Japanese/English livestream viewer comments**, then integrate it into an independently testable version of the existing AI Livestream demo. Compare it fairly against the existing 1.7B general-purpose model on quality, latency, download size and memory, including mobile feasibility.

This is an **experiment**, not a presumption that a fine-tuned small model will outperform a 1.7B model or that a Pixel 7a will run it well.

## Implementation discretion

**The implementation agent chooses the method and carries it out.** Do not mandate a particular base model, parameter count, dataset, training framework, LoRA/QLoRA technique, distillation strategy, optimizer, number of examples, or quantization/runtime. The agent should evaluate realistic options, justify a tractable choice, and perform the fine-tuning/adaptation and browser deployment.

- Use a small model that can plausibly run locally in a phone browser while generating short, natural Japanese comments. Support English too if feasible, without sacrificing the key Japanese use case.
- Build and curate a task-appropriate dataset of *spoken utterance / brief recent conversational context → natural viewer comment* examples, including questions, short reactions, different voices, topic changes, silence/non-response, ASR errors, repetition and cases that must not produce misleading content.
- Training data and model weights must have compatible licenses and provenance. Avoid scraping copyrighted chat logs or using real user audio/transcripts without explicit permission. If synthetic teacher-model data is used, comply with model/provider terms and evaluate contamination/quality; do not send real user media to a teacher API.
- Training may occur offline during development; **all inference in the published demo remains entirely local to the browser**.
- Prefer free/local compute and low-cost tooling. **Do not enable paid training/inference services, purchase GPU capacity, or change the Cloudflare plan/secrets without explicit user approval.** Clearly disclose training hardware/time limitations if present.
- Produce a real fine-tuned model/adaptation artifact (not merely changed prompting, hardcoded comments or a nominal model ID). Make artifacts, scripts and reproduction steps available in a maintainable manner: pin revisions/checksums, document training method and data, and host assets suitably for static deployment without checking enormous binary weights into the repository.
- Consider a quantized or otherwise deployable browser format (WebGPU/WebAssembly) and verify it is supported on the target runtime. Do not claim that a desktop-only converted model is mobile-ready.

## Scope: isolate the LLM experiment

- [ ] Keep the existing Whisper speech-recognition model, six-second audio sampling strategy, overall camera behavior, virtual viewer/like/subscribe simulation, and minimalist YouTube-inspired layout **unchanged unless an essential compatibility fix is needed**. Avoid simultaneous ASR/camera/audience/cadence refactors so the result is attributable to the model change.
- [ ] Integrate the trained model as the new experimental comment generator in the live demo, **with a unobtrusive rollback/comparison route** (for example a URL parameter such as `?model=baseline`); no additional visible settings, tech badges, marketing copy or explanatory text in normal mode.
- [ ] Preserve text-generation privacy: no speech/transcript/prompt/chat upload or cloud inference; only static runtime/model downloads may leave the browser.
- [ ] Preserve cancellation, memory/queue bounds, safety filtering, no invented visual observations, camera/mic stop cleanup and graceful unsupported-device behavior.
- [ ] Keep training-only tools out of the runtime website/normal Pages build; all existing unrelated Sandbox projects should continue working.

## Evaluation

- [ ] Establish baseline quality/latency using existing Japanese and English speech fixtures and new **held-out** examples not used in training or teacher selection. Include varied everyday topics and multi-turn fragments, not just a small collection of keywords.
- [ ] Measure and report relevance, naturalness, diversity, false claims, excessive repetition, valid-comment yield, and time to visible comment using a transparent reproducible rubric. Record representative examples and failures. Do not present filter acceptance rate alone as proof of higher quality.
- [ ] Compare initial download, cold/warm load, inference latency, peak memory, and user-visible camera responsiveness where measurable against the 1.7B baseline. Benchmarks on a Mac must be labeled as Mac results, not claimed Pixel 7a results.
- [ ] Add deterministic fixture tests for the training/inference integration, output quality bounds, browser loading, model choice/rollback and privacy. Use bounded real-model smoke tests where feasible without turning CI into a multi-GB download or requiring GPU hardware.
- [ ] Document any gaps (e.g. device/GPU incompatibility, Japanese ASR bottleneck) honestly. A model may be preferable in some dimensions but worse in others.

## Acceptance criteria

All acceptance criteria must be independently verifiable by an implementation agent in its available environment. **Manual Pixel 7a/Mac testing by the user is optional post-merge feedback and MUST NOT block completion or PR review.**

1. A real, reproducible task-specific fine-tuning/adaptation has been performed and documented, with an accessible trained artifact, licenses, data provenance and reproducibility instructions. A prompt-only change does not qualify.
2. The demo can load and use the trained model **entirely in the browser** to generate comments related to recognized speech; the original 1.7B model remains accessible for a nonintrusive A/B comparison or quick rollback.
3. The implementation supplies reproducible baseline-vs-trained results using held-out fixtures, including quality examples, accepted comments, resource/latency measurements and limitations. Any quality improvement is evidence-backed rather than asserted.
4. Model loading/inference failure is handled without leaking camera/microphone tracks, hanging the interface indefinitely, or silently switching to remote inference. Normal visual design and existing engagement features remain intact.
5. Automated tests of the new path and existing Sandbox build/gallery/browser regressions pass, with no real user device/human verification as a merge gate.

## Non-goals

No new remote AI API, paid backend or TURN service; no changing the voice recognizer, video resolution, virtual-audience rules, UI content, or general comment cadence as part of this experiment.
